public_comment.stated_role: resident; vice chair, master plan steering committee
public_comment.topic: Urges the school committee to prioritize renovating/replacing Turkey Hill Elementary, citing ADA/handicap accessibility issues and the approaching MSBA statement-of-interest window in January 2027.

Thanks the committee for pursuing the extra state education funding, argues the millionaire's-tax money is constitutionally for education, and describes her daughter's scheduling problems (no room for a PE class junior year) from prior cuts.

Shares her own review of ten years of cherry sheet data arguing state aid has never decreased year over year, praises Gilman's petition effort, and urges the select board to cooperate on the warrant article.
Asks whether the new part-time athletic director will also serve as vice principal, as the previous position-holder did.

budget_items.topic: Cherry sheet education-line increases, FY27 governor's budget vs. final budget
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair walked through the difference between the governor's initial FY27 local aid proposal and the final signed budget for chapter 70, charter tuition reimbursement, and smart growth school reimbursement. She noted charter tuition and smart growth are highly variable year to year while school choice receipts have generally been declining.

budget_items.topic: Total cherry sheet receipts increase
budget_items.what_was_said: The total increase across all cherry sheet receipt lines (education plus small increases in UGGA and aid for the visually impaired/elderly) was given as this figure.

budget_items.topic: State assessments/charges increase (school choice and charter sending tuition)
budget_items.what_was_said: School choice sending tuition decreased while charter school sending tuition increased, netting to this additional assessment amount, the only assessments that rose being education-related.

budget_items.topic: Net additional state aid available to the town
budget_items.what_was_said: Subtracting the extra assessments from the extra receipts yields the town's net additional state aid for FY27, framed as the basis for the school committee's funding request.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: maintenance of buildings to grounds contracted services
budget_items.what_was_said: Transfer to cover a grounds contracted-services overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: maintenance salaries to maintenance overtime
budget_items.what_was_said: Transfer to cover a maintenance overtime overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: custodian salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from middle and high school custodian lines to elementary and primary school custodian lines to cover overages.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: athletic security/detail
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from athletic transportation to special detail (police) at athletic events to cover an overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: regular transportation
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from heating charges to regular transportation; business manager said the transportation line had simply been budgeted too low the prior year, and it has since been revised for FY27.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: high school guidance salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from middle school guidance counselors to high school guidance counselor and secretary lines; attributed partly to costs from summer scheduling issues.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: high school substitutes
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from long-term substitutes to regular substitutes to cover an overage.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: high school principal/assistant principal salaries
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from a middle school administrative secretary line; described as a line that had been budgeted too low, now corrected for FY27.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: special education paraprofessionals and hospital tutoring
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from a high school special education resource room teacher line (attributed to a staff leave of absence) to hospital tutoring and special ed paraprofessional lines across several schools.

budget_items.topic: Line item transfer: superintendent general supplies
budget_items.what_was_said: Transferred from dues and meetings to general supplies, attributed to unused conference/meeting funds.

budget_items.topic: FY26 year-end budget spend rate
budget_items.what_was_said: The business manager reported total expenses came in at about this percentage of budget, with salaries still being finalized and expected to land close to but under 100%.

budget_items.topic: Prior-year budget overage (context for the shortfall crisis)
budget_items.what_was_said: Referencing the overage that caused a earlier-year budget crisis, a member asked what share of the budget it represented; the business manager estimated it at around 2.5%, expecting this year's number to be smaller.

budget_items.topic: LEAF grants (Lunenburg Education Accelerator Foundation)
budget_items.what_was_said: LEAF's first year of fundraising produced six grants for classroom/program items (sound system, erector sets, STEM materials, magazine subscriptions), totaling this amount.

budget_items.topic: Lunenburg Musicators donations
budget_items.what_was_said: The Musicators donated $300 for color guard uniforms/gloves (citing a tripling of band/color guard membership) and $1,213 to fund the middle school jazz band stipend.

budget_items.topic: Football helmets donation, withdrawn
budget_items.what_was_said: Football boosters had offered to buy extra helmets, but because helmets are integral to safety the district will pay for them instead, so that donation was withdrawn.

budget_items.topic: Football/cheer away-game transportation donation
budget_items.what_was_said: With transportation cut from the athletic budget, the football boosters will fund two buses for away games (football and cheerleaders), split into three separate donations to preserve some booster treasury funds for the season.

budget_items.topic: FY27 technology/infrastructure earmark from Senator Cronin's office
budget_items.what_was_said: The district received notice of a state earmark for system infrastructure upgrades; the superintendent will work with technology and buildings/grounds staff on a spending plan.

budget_items.topic: ESSER/Title grant allocations
budget_items.what_was_said: Title II and Title IV allocations were relatively flat ($28,443 and $15,19 as heard); Title I came in far higher than the $96,000 the district had budgeted for, at $193,820, reason unknown to the superintendent.

budget_items.topic: Warrant article amount for additional state aid to schools
budget_items.what_was_said: Gilman proposed increasing the previously-passed $350,000 warrant article to $418,000 (the legislature's increase to Lunenburg schools above the governor's budget) or as much as $475,000 (total town-wide increase); she noted the district also cut over $800,000 this year and that a further roughly $300,000 in one-time state money exists that she is not requesting.

budget_items.topic: Proposed use of the additional $68,000 (difference between $350,000 and $418,000)
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent proposed using the incremental funds to restore a certified occupational therapy assistant (COTA) position, needed in part due to a new unfunded state mandate eliminating school "cool down rooms."

budget_items.topic: Town stabilization/free cash funds, contrasted with the requested state aid
budget_items.what_was_said: Gilman stated the town holds over $9 million in its stabilization account and is also receiving more free cash, but said she is not asking for any of that one-time money, distinguishing it from the recurring state aid she is requesting.

budget_items.topic: Final FY27 warrant article amount for the September 3 special town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: The committee voted to amend its warrant article language to request this full amount of additional education receipts for the FY27 operating budget, rather than the previously voted $350,000.

budget_items.topic: Potential additional per-pupil state funding (millionaire's tax)
budget_items.what_was_said: Gilman described a further proposal from the governor for $100 million in millionaire's-tax funds for per-pupil aid, which could mean roughly $170,000-$175,000 more for the district if the legislature passes it; the superintendent cautioned it would not be enough to restore multiple lost positions.

budget_items.topic: Custodians' union (AFSCME Council 93) contract economics
budget_items.what_was_said: The new MOU gives custodians a 3.5% increase in FY27 and 2.5% increases in FY28 and FY29, adds longevity steps, converts longevity pay to flat dollar amounts ($500/$1,000/$1,250/$1,750 by years of service), and raises the clothing allowance to $455.

budget_items.topic: Athletic director / assistant principal staffing structure and cost
budget_items.what_was_said: The previously combined half-time athletic director/vice principal role (held by Miss Burns) has been split; the district plans two full-time assistant principals contingent on town meeting appropriating the funds, alongside a new half-time athletic director.

decisions.decision: The district, rather than the football boosters, will pay for extra football helmets, so that donation offer was withdrawn.

Rather than track two competing routes (the citizen petition and a separate school committee article), the committee agreed to take the language of the existing warrant article, amend it, and vote on it as the committee's own article, with Gilman stating she will not separately pursue funding through the citizen petition track.

The Athletic Advisory Committee will be restarted to help coordinate booster-club fundraising and ensure compliance with state/federal requirements; Tony and Mandy will serve on it along with volunteers Peter Beard and others.
The committee will put together an MSBA/Turkey Hill primer presentation for itself and the public ahead of beginning the formal MSBA process.

No regular meeting is planned for August, though a Zoom meeting may be called if needed for line item transfers; the committee will otherwise meet next at a finance committee meeting and then the day before the September 3 special town meeting.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg School Committee reviewed FY26 year-end line item transfers, approved several donations (LEAF grants, Musicators, football boosters), heard a detailed presentation on additional FY27 state aid via the cherry sheet, and voted to amend its warrant article for the September 3 "extra special" town meeting from $350,000 to $418,056 in additional state education aid. It also voted to sign a letter to the legislature supporting a further $100 million per-pupil funding proposal, ratified a new custodians' union contract, heard the superintendent's report on hiring and grants, approved a 300th-anniversary fireworks proposal, and discussed the long MSBA process facing Turkey Hill Elementary.
